chunks: Abu Basir asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who has eight hundred dirhams, is a cobbler, and has many dependents: may he take from zakat? So he said:

O Abu Muhammad, does he make profit from his dirhams enough to provide sustenance for his dependents and still have a surplus? He said: Yes. He said: How much surplus does he have? He said: I do not know. He said: If what remains beyond sustenance equals half of the sustenance, then he should not take zakat; but if it is less than half of the sustenance, he may take zakat.

He said: I said, then is zakat due upon his wealth? He said: Yes. He said: I said, how should he act? He said: He should use it to provide more amply for his dependents in their food and clothing, and keep some of it to hand over to others besides them. And whatever he takes from zakat, he should distribute it among his dependents until he brings them up to the level of the people.

key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: zakat, the obligatory alms discussed here both as something taken and something due
key_terms.خَفَّافٌ: cobbler, indicating his trade and livelihood
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: dirham, the unit of wealth mentioned in assessing the man’s means
key_terms.عِيَالٌ: dependents or family members whom he must support
key_terms.كِسْوَتِهِمْ: their clothing, part of the family’s essential support
key_terms.يَفْضُلُ: to remain in surplus beyond necessary expenses

ai.seo_question: Can a person with savings and a trade still receive zakat if he has many dependents?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on when a working man with some capital and many dependents may still receive zakat. The criterion is whether his profit exceeds his family’s sustenance by a significant margin, while also affirming that zakat may still be due on his wealth and should be used to support his dependents adequately.
